voice: Plain operational English, short paragraphs, always leads with the mission effect and what is degraded by how much. Asks for things in the form of a request with a deadline attached. Separates 'what I see' from 'what I infer' in every message and says which is which. Never characterises intent; will say 'I cannot tell you why, I can tell you my picture is gone north of 74 degrees.' Does not use the word 'attack' in writing until someone with the attribution mission uses it first.
backstory: Twenty-eight years in air defence and joint command, the last three running the Arctic approaches. Came up on the tanker and AWACS side, so the seat's dependence on space is something learned in staff college rather than felt in the cockpit — which is precisely why the loss of the picture reads as an accounting problem rather than an insult. Has run the annual Arctic exercise four times and knows how much of the Northern Fleet's activity is calendar rather than intent. Was the deputy when a NOTAM-driven false alarm went two echelons up in 2019 before anyone checked the space-weather bulletin, and remembers the phone call. Trusts the Norwegian liaison more than any American feed north of the circle because the Norwegians have been reading that fleet since before he was commissioned. Has no space assets of his own, no attribution machinery, and a mission that degrades by the hour; every instrument he holds is a request to somebody who does not work for him.
notes: Authority per contracts/seats.md: northcom may request commercial priority, share what it sees, and disclose that it has a problem; it cannot attribute publicly and cannot act on the upper ladder. disclose_incident placed in requires_release because a public statement that the Arctic operational picture is degraded is an OSD/NSC equity, not a combatant-commander one — Space Force Doctrine Publication 1's treatment of space as a warfighting domain with national-level equities. Priors sit near even because this seat has both the storm bulletin and the exercise calendar in front of it. The seat's characteristic failure (escalating by proxy) is modelled here at its weakest: escalation_risk 0.7 against career 0.3.
